metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that are consistent with the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. For each trial, it identifies the first discriminating cue (in order of descending validity) and checks if the subject chose the option favored by that cue. Because the experimental design intentionally pits TTB against WADD on 80% of the trials (where the highest-validity discriminating cue favors one option but the sum of all lower-validity cues favors the other), data simulated under TTB will yield a score close to 1.0 (subject to noise), while data simulated under WADD will yield a score well below 0.5. This provides a massive, reliable separation between the two theories.

This metric isolates 'compensatory' trials where the Take The Best (TTB) model and the Weighted Additive (WADD) model make opposing predictions. TTB strictly follows the single highest discriminating cue, whereas WADD integrates all cues, allowing lower-validity cues to compensate. By calculating the proportion of choices that align with TTB specifically on these conflicting trials, we can cleanly separate the two theories. TTB will produce a score near 1.0, while WADD will produce a score considerably lower (often near 0.0, depending on the exact subjective feature weights).
